Re: Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial  
Requested service: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion at C5-C6  
CPT: 22551  
Reference number: POC-B70A1741F9-18248  
Denial notice date: August 15, 2026

To Wellpoint Appeals:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the requested C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The clinical record demonstrates that the MRI findings are anatomically consistent with my symptoms, examination findings, and neurologic deficit, and that reasonable conservative treatment has failed.

The relevant clinical evidence is as follows:

- I have had progressive neck pain for nine months, unrelieved by rest.
- I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from April 12, 2026, through July 5, 2026. I completed 20 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 27, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief.
- A cervical MRI performed on July 18, 2026, shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root.
- I have radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, with weakness.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- The C5-C6 MRI abnormality, right C6 nerve-root compression, right-sided symptoms, and corresponding neurologic deficit are concordant in level and side. The imaging is therefore not an incidental finding; it identifies a structural lesion that explains the persistent radiculopathy and weakness.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance use. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

The requested procedure is intended to remove the C5-C6 disc herniation and decompress the compressed C6 nerve root, with fusion to stabilize the treated level. The record supports medical necessity because I have persistent and progressive symptoms, objective neurologic impairment, imaging-confirmed nerve-root compression, and inadequate response to extended nonoperative treatment.

The denial letter does not identify the specific Wellpoint medical policy, clinical guideline, policy number, version, effective date, or criterion that the reviewer found unsatisfied. I have not quoted plan policy language because the denial did not identify the governing document, and the publicly available Carelon guideline located during research was not confirmed as the guideline adopted for this New Jersey Commercial/ACA plan. Please provide the exact policy or clinical review criteria applied to this request, including its title, identifier, version or effective date, plan adoption status, and the specific reason the July 18, 2026, MRI was considered insufficient.

Please conduct a complete appeal review of the submitted records, including the MRI report and images, physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection history, examination findings, and the treating surgeon’s clinical documentation. Please also arrange a peer-to-peer discussion with Lindqvist, MD, if available under the applicable appeal process.

Based on the documented C5-C6 disc herniation, severe right foraminal narrowing, C6 nerve-root compression, corresponding neurologic deficit, progressive symptoms, and failed conservative treatment, I request that Wellpoint overturn the denial and authorize CPT 22551.

Please send the appeal determination and the specific clinical rationale in writing. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise if any additional information is required.

Sincerely,

Harper Kimura  
Member ID: W631917869  
Reference number: POC-B70A1741F9-18248
